subject: Post-call executive recap: AuroraTech discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Brian Chen <brian.chen@auroratech.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.m@auroratech.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-03-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call executive recap: AuroraTech discovery & next steps

Hi Brian / Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick executive-level recap from our call and proposed next steps so your leadership and procurement teams have a clear path forward. I’ve summarized the business outcomes, primary risks you raised, and the suggested procurement path below.

Key business outcomes AuroraTech is targeting
- Reduce customer support ticket triage time by 60% over 6 months via automated summarization + intent routing.
- Improve self-serve conversion by surfacing contextual product recommendations in-app.
- Lower inference cost per 1k queries through batching and prefix caching.

Primary pain points you confirmed
- High latency and unpredictable cost on current in-house model serving stack (esp. at peak loads).
- Lack of fine-grained observability to tie token costs to routes/features.
- Procurement preference for a vendor that can support private VPC deployment and provide SOC 2 evidence.

Risks & mitigation
- Data residency / security: Redwood Private (VPC) + KMS integration available; we will provide SOC 2 artifacts and network diagrams. (See attached SOC2 package.)
- Integration lift: we propose a two-week technical pilot (scope below) with a dedicated solutions engineer to accelerate POC.
- Cost predictability: recommend Dedicated reserved pool + automatic fallback policy to cap latency; we’ll share modeled TCO based on your 3M qpm estimate.

Procurement path & timeline (suggested)
1) Technical deep dive + security questionnaire answered — target: Mar 29
2) 4-week pilot (private deployment or dedicated instance) — Apr 5 start
3) Procurement & SOW negotiation — mid-April to early May
4) Production rollout phased by product line — June onwards

Immediate next steps (action owners)
- Brian / Sofia: Confirm procurement contact (Carlos?) and pilot approval path by EOW (Mar 25).
- AuroraTech: Share security contact email and any compliance checklist items you want prioritized.
- Redwood (Marissa): Send pilot scope, pricing grid, and SOC 2 evidence. [Attachments listed below].
- Redwood (Aditya): Schedule technical deep dive the week of Mar 29.

Attachments
- AuroraTech-Discovery-Summary.pdf (summary of pain/goals & call notes) [Attachment]
- redwood-enterprise-pricing-v2.xlsx (pilot and Dedicated pricing options) [Attachment]
- soc2-evidence-package.zip (redwood SOC 2 artifacts, SOC 2 report stub) [Attachment]

If helpful I can brief your CEO/CTO directly next week for an executive alignment call — happy to set that up.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0124
[Attachment: AuroraTech-Discovery-Summary.pdf]

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap and proposed timeline. Both Sofia and I are aligned on the business outcomes and the risks you called out. A few quick clarifications: 
- Confirmed: Carlos Ruiz (cc’d) is our procurement lead and will own contractual review.
- Security: I’ll ask our InfoSec to provide a high-level list of must-have controls; would you be able to return answers in 3 business days after we send?
- Pilot: We prefer a private VPC pilot. Can you confirm estimated infra lead time for a VPC-based pilot (hours/days)?

We’re generally OK with the proposed timing. I’ll route this to Carlos and he’ll coordinate procurement milestones.

—Brian
